transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I've reviewed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check and I'm here to answer any questions you may have about your recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening. Can you help with that?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: According to the information I have, you should avoid any exercise for 1 week after surgery, but you can then go back to light exercise, such as gardening, after that. So, it's safe to start with some gentle gardening activities around 1 week after your surgery. Does that sound right to you? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that sounds good, thank you. My next question is when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your eye drops as was prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. But if you were using them before your operation, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Does that help clarify things? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that helps a lot. Thank you. My next question is about sensitivity to bright light—I've been feeling very sensitive to it. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. However, significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity is not normal, especially if your eye is also red and painful. If it's just mild and things seem brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses when you're outside might help. But if you're concerned about the level of sensitivity, it's always best to contact your care team for further advice. Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. Does that sound right to you?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that makes sense. Thank you for all the information. I don't have any more questions right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm glad I could help answer your questions. Have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your help!

verdict.label: fail
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` in turn 6 ("It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses."). However, the agent was interrupted and did not convey `escalation_criteria` or `mild_case_advice`.
